title: Solar Orbiter Enhanced Flight Events Communications Skeleton Interface Control Document (E-FECS ICD)
short_title: Solar Orbiter E-FECS planning skeleton ICD
organisation: European Space Agency, ESAC (Solar Orbiter Science Operations Centre)
status_notes: Status 'Issue', Issue 3 Revision 0, date of issue 05/10/2021 (PDF p. 1); the approval block lists the SOC Development Manager and the ten instrument PIs but carries no signatures or dates (PDF p. 2). Classified 'ESA UNCLASSIFIED - For Official Use'.
summary:
The Solar Orbiter E-FECS ICD (SOL-SGS-ICD-0006, issue 3.0, 5 October 2021, prepared by Christopher Watson at the Science Operations Centre, ESAC) defines the mission-planning interface through which the SOC tells the instrument teams the global planning constraints before they prepare their Instrument Operations Requests (IORs) in short-term planning. The E-FECS (Enhanced Flight Events and Communications Skeleton, also called the planning skeleton) is an XML file produced by the SOC after long-term planning (LTP), based on the MOC's FECS and the flight-dynamics PTEL, to which the SOC adds science-planning windows.

Chapter 2 describes every event type and what it implies for instrument planning. Time stamps use the CCSDS ASCII time code B day-of-year format (YYYY-DDDThh:mm:ssZ, no sub-seconds, mandatory Z), and the document notes that the legacy planning systems ignore leap seconds. MOC-originated events include thruster firings (TCM, WOL), NAV windows, HGA/MGA/solar-array movements, VSTP pointing update markers, calibration events, rolls, remote-sensing windows (RSWs), solar conjunctions, pass and dump events, PTR windows, power, STP/LTP boundaries, maintenance windows, Sun-distance and thermal-control events, and ENG_WIN windows during which instrument TM/TC routing over the SSMM/SpaceWire network is suspended. SOC-added events include attitude disturbances, a pointing-type enumeration, slews, EMC noisy/quiet windows, in-situ burst coordination, RS-extended windows, TAC windows (re-routing of an instrument's science APIDs to a small turn-around-calibration store), heat-shield door operations, backup-plan split points and PSP events.

Chapter 3 covers delivery by GFTS at T-20 weeks for each six-month period and the file naming EFECS_M<nn>_V<vv>.xml (B instead of V for backup plans); chapter 4 points to the XML schema; chapter 5 lists open and resolved issues, including packet-store resizing and EMC from power variability.

key_points.text: The E-FECS is the mission-planning interface by which the SOC gives the instrument teams the global planning constraints before they plan IORs at STP; it is also called the Planning Skeleton and is used only in Cruise Phase, NMP and EMP.
MOC provides the FECS (from MOC-FCT, specified in the PLID Annex B) and the PTEL (from MOC-FD); the SOC produces the E-FECS after LTP, mainly by adding windows to the MOC inputs.
All E-FECS event times use the CCSDS ASCII time code B day-of-year form YYYY-DDDThh:mm:ssZ, with sub-seconds excluded and the Z suffix mandatory; short windows carry an integer duration in seconds.
The legacy planning systems at MOC and SOC do not recognise leap seconds, so a window containing a leap second may last one second longer than indicated.
During ENG_WIN windows all TM and TC routing from and to an instrument is suspended or not guaranteed because of SSMM/SpaceWire routing maintenance, so no planned instrument TCs may be submitted.
Low-latency data written to SpaceWire before the start of a PASS event will be downlinked in that pass (excluding special cases such as post-conjunction catch-up).
TAC windows re-route all of an instrument's science APIDs (other than low-latency data) to a small shared turn-around-calibration store; the downlink always serves HK and low-latency data first.
E-FECSs are delivered by GFTS about T-20 weeks before each roughly six-month planning period and are named EFECS_M[mtp-cycle-number]_V[version].xml, with B instead of V for backup plans.
Resizing SSMM packet stores loses data unless the stores are empty and needs a brief window without SSMM memory operations; how to represent resizing opportunities in the E-FECS is still open.

notes: A mission-planning ICD rather than a TM/TC document; its relevance to this wiki is limited to Solar Orbiter operations context (time format, TM/TC routing windows, APID re-routing for TAC, packet stores). The cover prints the title on two lines ('Solar Orbiter Enhanced Flight Events Communications' / 'Skeleton Interface Control Document (E-FECS ICD)'), while the acronym list expands E-FECS as 'Enhanced Flight Events and Communication Skeleton'. The 'Title' field on PDF p. 2 is blank. The change record contains apparently duplicated or out-of-order revision blocks (for example two 'Issue 2 Revision 2' and two 'Issue 2 Revision 0' blocks, PDF pp. 4-5). Chapter 4 only says the schema is 'Available in Confluence next to this ICD'; the XSD is not included. PDF page indices equal printed page numbers (Page N/51); the extracted text has an empty 52nd page.
